bug_semantics: The Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire vector-store converters serialize a caller-supplied Filter.Key into a Lucene-style query string. Their escaping left tab, LF, CR, and U+3000 ideographic space unescaped, so a key can introduce token boundaries and operators such as OR; the resulting string is passed to the backend query parser, allowing an attacker to replace the intended metadata predicate with arbitrary query clauses.
flaw_origin: Commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627 first added an affected backend and the causal pattern: ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.doKey() appended the metadata-prefixed Filter.Key directly to the query string with only trim(), while ElasticsearchVectorStore supplied that converted string to Elasticsearch queryString(). OpenSearch later copied the affected converter in 46e47849cec4b8a6fffbd13997f3cce4f886347b, and GemFire added the same kind of filter-query path in 833a856f51090f0eb98332db2341ce7a107af1fd. Later shared-converter refactors and partial escaping changed the location and reduced the character set but did not create the vulnerability or close the whitespace bypass.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627 shows human author Jemin Huh <hjm1980@gmail.com> and human committer Christian Tzolov <ctzolov@vmware.com>; the commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47835 states that special characters could force arbitrary queries in Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire VectorDB and identifies affected Spring AI 1.0.0-1.0.8 and 1.1.0-1.1.7, fixed in 1.0.9 and 1.1.8; GHSA references direct commits https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/commit/2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991 and https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/commit/9787991aa1ed92c511131ddf4e142bd94051e6e7. In the validated full-history clone, git log -L 86,95:vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java 9334d7d... resolves the raw doKey implementation to the new-file commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627; git log -S 'context.append(prefixedIdentifier.trim()).append(":");' confirms 9334d7d... added that statement and later fc1f92d11cacc79bdf8d41eb7f941a64fdf67482 only moved/refactored it. The BIC also added vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchVectorStore.java, whose getElasticsearchSimilarityQuery() sends getElasticsearchQueryString(filterExpression) into queryString(...). Direct parent-tree check `git cat-file -e 8e50802eb8dd9044c15d7e75ad94ae618dca5c12:vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java` fails because the path is absent, while the BIC adds it from /dev/null. GitHub's commit-to-pulls API returns [] for 9334d7d..., and the one-parent commit object contains the actual feature diff, so there is no squash member history to substitute. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds from 9334d7d... to v1.0.0 (fcd2803f36f35939c20ed152c9c1b0863fa35dcf), v1.1.0 (fa4c61eabeba0a69147b3c00a3b50380c1f25a75), and both fixes. At v1.0.8, AbstractFilterExpressionConverter.emitLuceneString() escapes ordinary space and Lucene punctuation but not tab/LF/CR/U+3000, and Elasticsearch doKey() routes the metadata field path through that helper. Direct fix 2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991 adds cases for '\t', '\n', '\r', and '\u3000' plus regression tests for all three stores; its equivalent 1.0.x backport is 9787991aa1ed92c511131ddf4e142bd94051e6e7. `git tag --contains` maps 2b20cfc... to v1.1.8 and 9787991... to v1.0.9; ancestry checks place neither fix in v1.1.7/v1.0.8 respectively, and place each in its patched tag.
reasoning: The security boundary is the construction of a backend query string, not merely the later helper method. The smallest affected-history commit that first made attacker-controlled metadata keys reach such a sink is 9334d7d..., which simultaneously introduced the Elasticsearch converter's unescaped doKey() and the queryString sink. The earlier similar Azure converter is not the BIC for this advisory because it enforces an allowedIdentifierNames whitelist and is not one of the affected products; 9334d7d... removed that safety in the newly affected backend. OpenSearch and GemFire are later ports of the same causal design. Refactors in 2026 centralized escaping and a partial hardening added ordinary-space handling, but the vulnerable capability already existed and the last vulnerable tags still failed to escape alternate whitespace. Both supported release lines then received the same four-character escaping patch at the documented fixed boundaries. The immediate parent lacks the affected converter and sink, the BIC predates both affected version lines, and the BIC commit object has no AI attribution signal; therefore the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
